messages:
oliver: quick alert — during today's canary we got a big burst of SLO notifications even though many tenants had quiet windows configured. saw duplicates in oncall channel.
neha: I noticed that too. looks like notify-worker used an old routing snapshot.
sam: why would snapshot be stale? TTL is 2m but we pushed policy label changes in canary.
rachel: confirm: notify-service checks quiet windows on emit, but fanout happens later in worker which used cached routing. mismatch => sends.
oliver: simple mitigation idea: invalidate routing cache on policy update events and lower TTL to ~15s for now.
neha: agree for emergency. also add a quick guard in worker: re-check quiet-window before each send.
sam: that guard changes internal contract (worker calling console metadata) — need to version the internal API. but we can add it as additive check.
rachel: telemetry gap made debugging harder. we don't have per-tenant fanout counters. add metric notify.fanout.count with tenant and policy tags.
oliver: and a delivery_status field on events: sent, skipped_quiet_window, dropped_quota. UI can reflect that.
neha: rollout plan: 1) metrics + tagging (safe) 2) short TTL + cache invalidation (emergency) 3) add send-time guard and delivery_status (API addition) 4) dashboard panels for delivery_status by tenant.
sam: ops: when invalidating caches, stagger restarts with jitter to avoid thundering herd.
devops-bot: Deploy bot: scheduled rolling restart of notify-worker initiated by neha at 2024-02-18T15:02:00Z.
rachel: I'll open the PR for metrics and a dashboard patch. oliver can you file the API doc issue for delivery_status?
oliver: on it. will also add sampling for metrics during high QPS (safety cap).
neha: ok pushing emergency changes now. will post status.
sam: thanks — once metrics land we can make a burn-rate alert for skipped_vs_sent spikes to catch regressions.
